name: Kao Data Manchester — KMAN-01, Stockport

book_concentration.rationale: Single 40MW campus at Kenwood Point, Stockport — Kao Data's only Northern England site and the region's largest planned facility.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Under-construction campus with on-site HV substation for national-grid import, but firm/non-firm connection terms are not publicly disclosed.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Single site in Greater Manchester (Northern Powergrid area), geographically separate from the constrained Slough/Docklands data-centre clusters.

trigger_gap.rationale: No disclosed availability or parametric curtailment cover; assumed damage-only property protection for a pre-operational build.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: £350m multi-year build targeting operations from 2026–2027 against negligible curtailment history for this new Northern hub.

data_monitoring.rationale: Established UK colocation operator with DCIM across existing campuses, but no published site telemetry yet for the pre-operational Manchester build.

product_fit.rationale: Planning specifies HVO-fuelled standby generators and NVIDIA DGX-Ready AI design, raising physical resilience though no insurance availability product is disclosed.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Asset-level entity without dedicated insurance underwriting capability.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Specialist private colocation developer (~160MW+ UK portfolio) funding a £350m greenfield campus without hyperscaler-scale balance-sheet depth.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Physical asset, not a risk-pricing or underwriting entity.

notes: KMAN-01 at Kenwood Point, Reddish, Stockport SK5 6PH; 40MW / 4,000+ racks, £350m; broke ground Oct 2024, ops targeted 2026–Q3 2027; on-site HV substation; HVO backup; BREEAM Excellent, PUE ~1.2; NVIDIA DGX-Ready; Northern England's largest planned DC; DNO Northern Powergrid region.

name: Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm — Moray Firth, Scotland
parent_group: SSE Renewables / Red Rock Power / TRIG / Equitix (JV)

book_concentration.rationale: Single 588 MW site with 84 turbines concentrates Moray Firth offshore generation value in one development.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Located behind key thermal transmission constraint boundaries; regularly curtailed via Balancing Mechanism since 2021 with Ofgem TCLC enforcement.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Exports from northern Scotland behind B4/B6 boundaries alongside Moray East/West and other Scottish wind, creating highly correlated constraint exposure.

trigger_gap.rationale: Balancing Mechanism constraint compensation is not availability or parametric cover against revenue loss from curtailment.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: Multi-decade CfD/investment-contract asset against a rapidly worsening Scottish boundary curtailment regime.

data_monitoring.rationale: Utility-scale offshore SCADA with documented high-volume Balancing Mechanism constraint dispatch.

product_fit.rationale: No evidence of curtailment or parametric insurance cover at asset level.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Generation asset without dedicated insurance underwriting capability.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Backed by SSE Renewables (FTSE-listed SSE plc) plus listed infrastructure funds TRIG and Equitix.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Generation asset, not an insurance pricing entity.

notes: 588 MW (84×7 MW) Outer Moray Firth; operational June 2019; O&M Wick; SSE Renewables 40% / Red Rock 25% / TRIG 17.5% / Equitix 17.5%; £33.14m Ofgem TCLC redress 2024 for excessive BM bid pricing when curtailed.

name: Race Bank Offshore Wind Farm — North Sea

book_concentration.rationale: Single 573 MW Round 2 site with 91 turbines concentrates generation value on one North Sea sandbank.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Firm 573 MW transmission entry capacity at Walpole but tracked in REF constraint-payment data when export circuits constrain output.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Shares east-coast North Sea export corridor with Hornsea, East Anglia and other offshore wind behind common transmission boundaries.

trigger_gap.rationale: Constraint Balancing Mechanism payments compensate marginal losses but are not availability or parametric cover.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: Long-lived ROC-era asset against a worsening east-coast constraint-payment regime as more North Sea wind connects.

data_monitoring.rationale: Full offshore SCADA with interlink redundancy design and documented Balancing Mechanism participation.

product_fit.rationale: No evidence of curtailment or parametric insurance cover at asset level.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Generation asset without dedicated insurance underwriting capability.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Majority-owned by Ørsted with Macquarie European Infrastructure Fund and Sumitomo as institutional co-investors.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Generation asset, not an insurance pricing entity.

notes: 573 MW (91×6 MW Siemens Gamesa) ~27 km off Norfolk/Lincolnshire; commissioned Feb 2018; 1.8 ROCs/MWh; export to National Grid Walpole; Ørsted 50% / Macquarie 37.5% / Sumitomo 12.5%; 220 kV interlink allows 50% export during single-circuit outage.

name: Walney Extension Offshore Wind Farm — Irish Sea

book_concentration.rationale: Single 659 MW site with 87 turbines concentrates Irish Sea offshore generation in one extension development.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Two-phase CfD-backed project with firm 400 kV connection at Middleton Heysham, though REF tracks periodic constraint payments.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Co-located Irish Sea cluster with Walney 1/2 and West of Duddon Sands sharing the Barrow/Middleton export boundary.

trigger_gap.rationale: No evidence of curtailment or availability parametric cover; assumed damage-only renewable property protection.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: 25-year CfD/asset horizon against emerging Irish Sea export constraints as Ørsted Barrow hub exceeds 1.5 GW.

data_monitoring.rationale: Utility-scale offshore SCADA with 220 kV interlink redundancy and active grid balancing dispatch.

product_fit.rationale: No evidence of curtailment or parametric insurance cover at asset level.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Generation asset without dedicated insurance underwriting capability.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Majority-owned by Ørsted with Danish pension-fund partners AIP Management and PFA providing institutional backing.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Generation asset, not an insurance pricing entity.

notes: 659 MW (87 turbines: 40 MHI Vestas 8 MW + 47 Siemens 7 MW) ~19 km off Cumbria; inaugurated Sep 2018; CfD phases WOW03/04; export via Middleton 400 kV Heysham; Ørsted 50% / AIP 25% / PFA 25%; world's largest OWF at commissioning.

name: Pen y Cymoedd Wind Energy + Storage — South Wales

book_concentration.rationale: Single 228 MW onshore site with 76 turbines concentrates Wales's largest onshore wind book on one Forestry Commission estate.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Fully operational onshore wind with firm grid export via dedicated 400 kV National Grid substation; REF tracks occasional constraint payments.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Single South Wales GSP in the Upper Afan Valley, away from constrained Scottish or Slough clusters.

trigger_gap.rationale: No evidence of curtailment or availability parametric cover; assumed damage-only renewable property protection.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: 25-year operational life and £400m project finance against evolving UK curtailment and grid-charging regime.

data_monitoring.rationale: Co-located 22 MW Battery@PyC provides sub-second Enhanced Frequency Response telemetry to National Grid.

product_fit.rationale: No insurance cover known, but co-located 22 MW lithium-ion BESS raises grid-resilience versus wind-only sites.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Generation asset without dedicated insurance underwriting capability.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Wholly owned by Vattenfall AB, a major European utility with substantial balance-sheet depth.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Generation asset, not an insurance pricing entity.

notes: 228 MW (76×3 MW Siemens) Upper Afan Valley, Neath Port Talbot/Rhondda Cynon Taf; operational 2017; co-located Battery@PyC 22 MW lithium-ion BESS (May 2018, EFR to National Grid)—no evidenced pumped-hydro scheme; exports via 400 kV NG substation; Vattenfall 100%.

name: SMS plc — Burwell BESS, Cambridgeshire

book_concentration.rationale: Single operational 50MW/56.2MWh site at Burwell, Cambridgeshire — one named asset concentrating value at a single East Anglia node.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Operational 132kV-connected BESS energised January 2022 earning balancing and ancillary services; transmission-linked firmness terms not publicly disclosed.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: All capacity behind one Burwell 132kV grid connection to the Burwell substation cluster — local outage or constraint affects the full 50MW asset.

trigger_gap.rationale: No public evidence of availability or parametric curtailment cover; revenue depends on merchant balancing and ancillary services not covered by damage-only insurance.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: Long-life infrastructure commissioned 2022 within SMS's multi-decade 620MW storage pipeline against a short and volatile BESS merchant revenue history.

data_monitoring.rationale: Trina Storage integrated system with modular PPC and SCADA for control, monitoring and optimisation; SMS independently operates balancing services post-energisation.

product_fit.rationale: No public evidence of availability or parametric insurance cover for this asset.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Asset owner and operator, not a risk carrier.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: SMS plc (LSE-listed smart-metering and infrastructure group) owns and operates the asset directly; credible but not utility-grade balance-sheet backing at single-site scale.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Asset owner, not an insurer; no curtailment-risk pricing capability evidenced.

notes: 50MW/56.2MWh lithium-ion BESS at Weirs Drove, Burwell, Cambridgeshire; energised January 2022; 132kV connection to Burwell substation; built by Ethical Power with Trina Storage supply; SMS-owned and operated — distinct from Gresham House GRID portfolio (no Burwell asset in GRID register).

name: EDF / Pivot Power — Kemsley BESS, Kent

book_concentration.rationale: Single operational 50MW/50MWh transmission-connected site at Kemsley substation, Kent — one named asset concentrating value at a single southeast node.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Among the first transmission-connected BESS on NETS, operational since October 2021 with EDF PowerShift optimisation; connection firmness not publicly disclosed.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: All 50MW sits behind a single Kemsley high-voltage transmission connection serving London and southeast load — correlated curtailment or outage hits the full asset.

trigger_gap.rationale: No public evidence of availability or parametric curtailment cover; revenue from Dynamic Containment, wholesale and Balancing Mechanism signals not covered by damage-only insurance.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: Operational since October 2021 within EDF Renewables' long-dated 10GW global storage target; short operating curtailment history against multi-decade infrastructure life.

data_monitoring.rationale: Wärtsilä GEMS digital energy platform with AI-enabled optimisation; EDF PowerShift route-to-market including Dynamic Containment and Balancing Mechanism participation.

product_fit.rationale: No public evidence of availability or parametric insurance cover.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Asset developer/operator under Pivot Power and EDF, not a risk carrier.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Owned by Pivot Power (EDF Renewables subsidiary) with EDF Group optimisation and Grid Code control-point management — major utility balance-sheet backing.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Asset owner, not an insurer; no curtailment-risk pricing capability at asset level.

notes: 50MW/50MWh lithium-ion BESS at Kemsley substation, Kent; activated October 2021; directly connected to National Grid high-voltage transmission network; Wärtsilä supply with GEMS platform; EDF PowerShift route-to-market; second Pivot Power Energy Superhub after Cowley — not Zenobe.
